messages:
alex.m: Heads-up — saw a big wave of small GPU pod evictions in eu-west1 starting ~00:45 UTC, looks correlated with a network heal event from the infra side.
priya.s: saw the same, roughly 00:46-00:50. pods kept moving between nodes and some tiny jobs got killed repeatedly.
matt: linking the event stream from infra-bot:
infra-bot: (automated) eu-west1 network heal started 2025-11-14T00:44:23Z, peering sessions flapped, BGP dedup applied, heal completed 00:48:12Z.
liam: that timeline matches K8s drains we triggered for nodes with NIC Rx errors. We did rolling cordon/drain to reprovision.
sara: the issue is the combination of drain + our strict inter-pod anti-affinity + gpu gang scheduling. Scheduler kept trying to pack full GPU pods but nodes had ephemeral free slots so it forced preemptions.
alex.m: exact symptom: repeated preempt cycle — pod A gets scheduled -> preempts cheap batch pod -> next scheduling round pack changes -> pod A gets preempted again when a different GPU gang arrives. Net effect = thrash and tokenized fragmentation.
priya.s: here's a snippet from scheduler logs around 00:47:
```
I1114 00:47:01.123 scheduler.go:220] binding pod default/model-trainer-7 to node gpu-az1-17
I1114 00:47:03.456 preemptor.go:87] preempted pod default/batch-worker-91 on node gpu-az1-12 for pod default/model-trainer-7
I1114 00:47:10.789 scheduler.go:301] detected node.network.rx_errs=high, cordon node gpu-az1-12
I1114 00:47:15.012 requeue.go:44] requeued pod default/model-trainer-7 due to node drain
```
matt: also saw inter-AZ traffic spike during that window — cross-az hops increased because pods were rescheduled to different racks while PVs were mounted remotely. NIC egress hit 80-90% on several nodes.
liam: cost hit was visible too — preemptions + cross-az egress spiked our per-token serving cost on that pool. rough back-of-envelope +12% for the hour.
sara: root causes (IMO): 1) network heal caused node-level Cordons 2) our scheduler packing heuristics don't treat temporary cordons as affinity to keep GPU gangs consolidated 3) anti-affinity + strict gang semantics force reshuffles.
priya.s: suggestion: add a short "grace keep" window after cordon heal where scheduler prefers existing az/rack placements and avoids preempting existing small pods for new GPU gangs. maybe 2-5 minutes.
alex.m: +1. small change: prefer nodes with recent cordon_uncordon events when binding, or penalize cross-az placements in first N minutes post-heal.
matt: throwing an experimental quick-fix: add a soft taint `transient-network-heal=true:NoSchedule` on nodes during heal and let kubelet remove after X minutes so scheduler won't shuffle immediately. downside: we need to ensure it doesn't block critical ops.
liam: we should also lower preempt aggressiveness during rolling infra maintenance windows. Canary knob: preempt_throttle_ms.
sara: operational runbook item: next time infra starts a heal, post to #eng-platform with exact node list and expected heal window + option to opt-out per-pool. That way platform teams can pin long-running GPU jobs.
priya.s: assigning follow-ups: @matt take quick patch for scheduler prefer-window, @liam add a metric for preempt_count per-gpu-pool, @alex.m coordinate runbook wording with infra.
alex.m: noted. I'll ping infra for the node list and add a short postmortem note.
infra-bot: (automated) Created incident INC-20251114-az1-network-heal, assignees: infra-networking, eng-platform.
priya.s: if anyone can whip up a short experiment today (non-prod) to simulate cordon/uncordon and validate the prefer-window heuristic that would help.
matt: can run a canary in eu-west1-nonprod around 14:00 UTC. will post results. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks all — main takeaways: avoid immediate reshuffles after network heals, soft-taint experiment, and runbook. keeping watch on cost delta metrics.
sara: adding doc link to scheduler design note — will update with prefer-window pseudo-code later.
